content.title: What if you die in the same condition as you are now?
content.subtitle: What will be the outcome?
content.body:
Close your eyes for a moment. Place your hand over your chest and listen to your heartbeat. This sound is not eternal; at a certain moment already decreed in the heavens, it will fall silent forever. The clothes you put on this morning… could they be the last clothes you wear before your shroud?

The True Self Revealed at the Moment of Death

A person spends their life nurturing certain things within, and in the final moments, what they truly lived for may be revealed. Someone immersed in drugs, music, entertainment, and obscenity may utter songs and meaningless words even when others try to make them recite the Shahadah. At the threshold of death, pretence no longer works. The true character of a lifetime is finally revealed.

Two Kinds of Death: The Righteous and the Sinful

Imagine two very different scenes. On one side is a fortunate servant—lost in the love of his Lord in the stillness of the night, his forehead resting on the prayer mat in sujood. In that very state, his soul gently rises to the heavens, leaving an ethereal smile upon his face.

On the other side is someone secretly immersed in sin when the Angel of Death arrives. The evidence of his wrongdoing remains behind. Would you have the courage to face Malakul Mawt at such a moment of ultimate humiliation?

The State of Your Death and the Day of Resurrection

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ warned: “Every servant will be resurrected in the very state in which he died.” (Sahih Muslim: 2878)

The one who dies in the ihram of Hajj will rise on the Day of Resurrection reciting the Talbiyah. But the one who dies with a bottle of wine in his hand or while signing a record of usurious dealings will stand before his Lord carrying the humiliation of that state.

The Door of Repentance Is Still Open

Has your heart trembled? Has guilt begun to stir within you? Then know this: that fear may be the light of a new life. Your Lord’s mercy is far greater than your sins. The fact that you are still breathing means the door of return is still open.

Allah Almighty says: “Say, O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of the mercy of Allah. Indeed, Allah forgives all sins. Surely, He is the Most Forgiving, the Most Merciful.” (Surah Az-Zumar: 53)

Prepare Today for a Beautiful Death

Weep for the mistakes of your past. Let your tears wash away the burden of your deeds. Raise your hands and cry out: “O my Master! You have seen my life as it was; now make my death beautiful. Do not take my soul while I am immersed in sin. Accept my final breath while I am lost in Your love, my forehead resting in a long, peaceful sujood.”

Remember, when a servant returns to his Lord weeping, it is beneath His majesty to send him away empty-handed. Return. The door is still open.
